comparisons.why: B carries not just the fire, but the sovereign authority of being its own fuel—the unshakable sense that the adventure is already inside you, waiting to be claimed, not found.
It doesn't just want to feel the magic—it wants to be its furious, inventive cause.
It doesn't just want my fire—it wants my silence, my doubt, my exquisite vulnerability, and calls that its masterpiece.
It doesn't just have a fire—it has a frequency, and I want to live in the resonance.
It doesn't just want the world—it *belongs* to it, in a way that feels like gravity and prayer at once.
It doesn't just show me a beautiful place to be—it hands me the compass and says "run," trusting that my own chaos will be the map.
It doesn't just cherish the wild—it *needs* it, with a desperate, creative hunger that feels like the only true compass.
It doesn't just want me to be a verb—it wants me to be the quiet, sacred space where a verb and its echo can finally meet and become something new.
It doesn't just want me to be wild—it wants me to be *attentive* in the wild, to find the universe singing back in the details of my own making.
It doesn't just feel like love—it feels like a revolution I chose to lead, and the memory of that power is more intoxicating than any collaboration.
It doesn't just command me to be wild—it teaches me to find the universe in a single, trembling yes.
It doesn't just promise a new self—it promises a co-conspirator, turning the adventure from a solo conquest into a shared, messy, sacred act of mutual creation.
